title: Polyarteritis nodosa: fibrinoid necrosis of medium muscular arteries
vignette: A 45-year-old woman comes to the office due to 3 days of progressive pain in the right upper quadrant, nausea, and vomiting. In the preceding year, the patient has had fatigue, weight loss, joint pain, and intermittent abdominal pain. Laboratory studies show increased blood urea nitrogen and serum creatinine. Right-upper-quadrant ultrasound shows no evidence of gallstones, but an inflamed gallbladder is present. The patient undergoes cholecystectomy, and subsequent biopsy of the submucosal gallbladder vessels (shown in the exhibit) reveals transmural inflammation with segmental fibrinoid necrosis of a medium-sized muscular artery. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

clues.text: fatigue, weight loss, joint pain, and intermittent abdominal pain
clues.note: Long-standing constitutional symptoms (fatigue, weight loss, arthralgia) plus abdominal pain suggest a systemic vasculitis rather than isolated gallbladder disease.

clues.text: increased blood urea nitrogen and serum creatinine
clues.note: Renal involvement (rising BUN/creatinine) is common in polyarteritis nodosa, which frequently attacks renal arteries.

clues.text: no evidence of gallstones, but an inflamed gallbladder
clues.note: Acalculous cholecystitis (inflamed gallbladder without stones) here results from ischemia of gallbladder arteries damaged by vasculitis.

clues.text: segmental fibrinoid necrosis of a medium-sized muscular artery
clues.note: Segmental transmural inflammation with fibrinoid necrosis of a medium-sized muscular artery is the diagnostic histology of polyarteritis nodosa.

whatMatters: Long-standing constitutional symptoms + renal involvement (↑BUN/creatinine) + acalculous cholecystitis + biopsy showing transmural inflammation with fibrinoid necrosis of a MEDIUM-sized muscular artery = polyarteritis nodosa (PAN). Answer D. PAN is a necrotizing medium-vessel vasculitis (kidney, GI, skin, nerves; lungs spared) that is NON-granulomatous and associated with hepatitis B.
strategy: Anchor on the biopsy: fibrinoid necrosis of a medium muscular artery with transmural inflammation = PAN. Reject antiphospholipid syndrome (bland thrombosis, no fibrinoid necrosis), granulomatosis with polyangiitis (granulomatous, ANCA+, lungs/upper airway), thromboangiitis obliterans (extremity vessels, young smokers, spares vessel wall), and angiodysplasia (dilated mucosal vessels, GI bleeding - not vasculitis).

eliminations.label: Angiodysplasia - dilated mucosal vessels, GI bleeding
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: tortuous dilated submucosal veins (e.g., cecum/right colon) causing GI bleeding. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is a vascular malformation, not a vasculitis; biopsy shows thin-walled dilated vessels, not fibrinoid necrosis with inflammation. ✅ Correct if: painless lower-GI bleeding with dilated mucosal vessels.

eliminations.label: Antiphospholipid-antibody syndrome - bland thrombosis
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: autoantibodies causing recurrent thrombosis/pregnancy loss. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: acute biopsy shows thrombosed vessels WITHOUT the transmural fibrinoid necrosis and neutrophilic inflammation of PAN. ✅ Correct if: recurrent clots/miscarriage with lupus anticoagulant/anticardiolipin antibodies.

eliminations.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis - granulomatous, ANCA+
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a c-ANCA (PR3)-positive small-vessel vasculitis of the upper airway, lungs, and kidneys. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is GRANULOMATOUS and lung-involving; PAN is non-granulomatous and spares the lungs, and this biopsy shows fibrinoid necrosis without granulomas. ✅ Correct if: sinusitis + lung nodules + glomerulonephritis with c-ANCA.

eliminations.label: Thromboangiitis obliterans - Buerger disease
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: segmental thrombosing vasculitis of small/medium extremity vessels in young smokers. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it spares the vessel wall (intact internal elastic lamina) with inflammatory thrombi in the extremities, not fibrinoid necrosis of visceral arteries. ✅ Correct if: distal extremity ischemia in a young heavy smoker.

reasoning: Constitutional symptoms + renal involvement + acalculous cholecystitis = systemic medium-vessel vasculitis
Biopsy: transmural inflammation with segmental fibrinoid necrosis of a medium muscular artery
This is the diagnostic histology of polyarteritis nodosa (non-granulomatous, spares lungs, hepatitis B association)
mechanism: Polyarteritis nodosa (PAN) is a systemic NECROTIZING vasculitis of small-to-medium-sized MUSCULAR arteries. Immune-mediated injury (classically associated with hepatitis B antigenemia/immune complexes) produces segmental, transmural inflammation with FIBRINOID NECROSIS of the arterial wall, weakening it and causing luminal narrowing/thrombosis (tissue ischemia) and microaneurysms (bead-like on angiography) that can rupture and bleed. Lesions are at different stages simultaneously (segmental). Clinically PAN affects the kidneys (renal artery involvement -> hypertension, rising creatinine), GI tract (mesenteric ischemia, here gallbladder-artery ischemia causing acalculous cholecystitis), skin, and peripheral nerves (mononeuritis multiplex), while classically SPARING the lungs. Critically, PAN is NON-granulomatous and typically ANCA-negative, distinguishing it from granulomatosis with polyangiitis. Treatment is corticosteroids ± cyclophosphamide (and antiviral therapy if hepatitis B-associated).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Rheum/CV > polyarteritis nodosa: medium-vessel necrotizing vasculitis, transmural fibrinoid necrosis, hepatitis B association, kidney/GI/skin/nerve, spares lung, non-granulomatous, ANCA-negative; string-of-beads microaneurysms.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: The medium-artery fibrinoid-necrosis biopsy with systemic + renal features pins PAN over the other vasculitides.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on fibrinoid necrosis, medium- vs small-vessel vasculitis, acalculous cholecystitis, mononeuritis multiplex, or granulomatous? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Antiphospholipid = bland thrombosis; GPA = granulomatous/ANCA+/lung; Buerger = extremity smokers; angiodysplasia = vascular malformation, not vasculitis.

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.text: On the histology exhibit: a medium muscular artery with amorphous pink (fibrinoid) necrosis and transmural inflammatory infiltrate. Anchor: 'fibrinoid necrosis of a medium artery = PAN.'

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: PAN = medium-vessel necrotizing vasculitis, hepatitis B, spares lungs, non-granulomatous; treat steroids ± cyclophosphamide.
